357 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Watches for the south shore of LI on Friday have 
been converted to Coastal Flood Advisories and the ending time 
for the Wind Advisory has been changed to 1 AM. The High Wind 
Warning remains unchanged.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A major coastal storm will bring high winds, rain, and
coastal flooding to the area through this evening. 

2) Widespread moderate to major coastal flooding likely during
the PM high tides. Minor to locally moderate impacts possible 
during Friday AM high tide. In addition, widespread beach 
flooding and dune erosion expected along the open water 
shorelines during the times of high tide, with localized 
overwashes possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The combination of anomalously strong high pressure over the
Northeast and low pressure tracking north across the Mid
Atlantic states will produce widespread rain and high winds
across the area through the first half tonight. An 80kt LLJ at 
925mb over the Delmarva region will lift north and east this
evening, passing across coastal sections this evening, with the
core moving across LI. This combined with low-level warming will
help to mix more of the momentum down to the surface with 40-50kt
winds likely at the coast until around 03Z before diminishing 
as the warm front moves into the area. A few higher gusts are
possible. The warm front will gradually lift north through the 
night along with rain and wind.

Heaviest rain will also coincide with the strongest winds this
evening, with even a rumble of thunder possible. Rainfall
amounts are still expected to be in the 1-2 range with localized
higher amounts up to 3 inches. The system is progressive and
hourly rates are unlikely to exceed an inch/hour. Any flooding
should be mainly of the minor nuisance variety. There is a low
probability of flash flooding.

Temperatures will gradually rise into the 50s through the 
night, especially with the passage of the warm front. A period 
of fog is also possible overnight as winds slacken with the 
warm front and increasing dew points. Low confidence at this 
time. Southerly winds do gradually increase after this lull 
from south to north.

Low pressure occludes tonight and passes to west late tonight
into Friday, passing to the north Friday night into Saturday.
The associated upper low passes to the northwest on Friday with
plenty of cloud cover and chances of showers. The best chance
will be to the north and west of NYC. Highs will top out in the
mid to upper 50s. MAV MOS and CONSALL are cooler and that is a
possibility with the cloud cover and the coverage of showers.
S-SW winds will gusts 25 to 30 mph. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Coastal flood warning remains up for tonight with the exception
of SE CT. The coastal flood watch for the south shore of LI for
Sunday has been converted to an advisory. Thus, a coastal flood
advisory is in effect for all locations on Sunday. 

While most locations need an additional foot to reach coastal 
flood benchmarks tonight, this will be offset by the highest
winds during the nighttime hours. Much of the surge guidance is
pointing to a 3 to 4 ft surge with widespread moderate to major
coastal flooding. In many cases, waters level have ticked up a
bit with our latest forecast. 

The storm surge will be driven by storm force ENE winds 
through the first half of tonight due to the strong pressure 
gradient between low pressure and high pressure to the north. 
Other areas of notes for significant impacts will be the Peconic
Bay area with funneling of surge towards the Peconic River, and
along W LI Sound shoreline with moderate water levels combined 
with high wave action. 

Surge up the tidally affected rivers (Hackensack, Hudson, and 
Passaic) will result in minor to moderate flooding as well,
especially during tonight's high tide cycle.

For the Friday AM high tides, winds switch to the southwest with
widespread minor likely. Localized moderate is possible in the
south shore back of bays of western LI. In general, the fcst has
been lowered except for the back bays where the SW flow may
slightly redistribute impacts.

For the oceanfront, breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result in
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high
tide. There is potential for localized overwashes, exacerbating
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind 
protective dunes. Along Western LI Sound and Twin Forks, 
breaking waves of 3 to 6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion
and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective
dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to 
shoreline and marina structures as well.

Heavy rain coinciding with the evening high tides could exacerbate
street flooding issues along the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /21Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
**HIGH IMPACT STORM TODAY AND TONIGHT**

A large storm will continue to move across the Mid Atlantic 
states today passing to the W late tonight. An associated warm 
front will approach this evening. 

MVFR cigs have developed across NYC metros and along the coast
with IFR conditions expected as rain becomes moderate to heavy 
at times this afternoon.

Winds out of the NE-ENE will increase into the afternoon to 
25-35 kt with G40- 50kt, strongest at the NYC metro and coastal 
terminals. Peak wind gusts could be a few kt higher. This will 
also be accompanied by easterly LLWS at 50-70kt at 1500-2000 ft 
AGL.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of strongest winds and heaviest rain timing could be off
a few hours.

Isolated thunder can not be ruled out this evening.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Friday through Tuesday... 

Friday: Chance of showers with MVFR cond, becoming VFR at 
night. SW winds G25-30kt, becoming W after midnight. 

Saturday: VFR. W winds G20-25kt, diminishing at night. 

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night: Showers likely with MVFR cond after midnight. 

Monday: Chance of morning showers with MVFR cond. SW winds G20-25kt, 
becoming W in the afternoon and NW at night.

Tuesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
No changes to the Gale and Storm Warnings. Seas on the ocean are 
modeled to build to around 20 ft at the height of the storm in the 
late aftn and eve, with waves on the Sound and the NY Harbor 
entrance up to around 10 ft. ENE winds will frequently gust in
the 50-60kt range this evening before weakening with a warm 
frontal passage later tonight.

Conditions improve a little on Fri, but a SW gale is likely on 
the ocean and maybe on some of the non-ocean waters as well.  
Winds diminish to SCA lvls on Sat in a westerly flow, and 
likely blw SCA lvls on Sun. A frontal sys on Mon could produce 
SW-W gales on the ocean with SCA conditions elsewhere.
